title: Kylian Mbappe leaves France vs. Morocco with apparent injury
content:
France star Kylian Mbappe appeared to suffer an injury scare during his nation’s World Cup quarter-final game against Morocco on Thursday afternoon.

Mbappe had already scored a sumptuous goal to open the scoring for France in the second half, which was then followed up by his team-mate Ousmane Dembele to give the French team a commanding 2-0 lead. Mbappe did, however, have a rare blip in the first half when his penalty, which he won when brought down by Morocco’s Manchester United defender Noussair Mazraoui, was saved by goalkeeper Yassine Bounou.

Mbappe’s goal tied him with Lionel Messi’s eight goals in the race for the World Cup Golden Boot.

However, Mbappe then exited the match in the 77th minute when, during open play and with Morocco in possession, he raised his arm to the bench and lay down on the floor. The Real Madrid forward did not appear in extreme distress but stretched out his right leg, accompanied by a medical professional. He waved to the crowd while walking off and gave high-fives to his team-mates on the bench.

Television footage subsequently showed Mbappe sitting on the France bench with ice resting on his right foot as the game continued.

France won the tie 2-0 and after the full-time whistle, Mbappe walked back onto the Gillette Stadium pitch smiling and hugging his team-mates. He was later jumping up and down, celebrating with the rest of his team in front of their fans, which is surely a welcome sight for France fans.

Mbappe has completed 90 minutes for France in the games against Senegal in the group stage and Paraguay in the round of 16, with coach Didier Deschamps affording the 27-year-old some precautionary rests for periods of games against Iraq, Norway and Sweden.

Further information will likely be provided on Mbappe by Deschamps in his post-match news conference, with France hoping he will be available for a semi-final in Dallas against Spain or Belgium on Tuesday, July 14.

The World Cup final will be played at MetLife Stadium on July 19.
